tagline: Up Route 100 from Waterbury to Stowe, under Mount Mansfield.
intro: Route 100 leaves Waterbury village and heads north up the valley. Three and a half miles on it passes the west side of Waterbury Center, near the east arm of the Waterbury Reservoir on the Little River, and six miles after that it reaches Stowe, in a broad valley with Mount Mansfield and the Green Mountains to the west and the Worcester Range to the east.

That stretch is only the start of the Green Mountain Byway, which goes on to circle 71 miles around the northern Green Mountains through Morristown, Hyde Park, Johnson and Cambridge, and over Smugglers' Notch.

moments.title: Waterbury
moments.text: Inscriptions on some village buildings claim to mark how high the water rose in the flood of 1927.

moments.title: Stowe
moments.text: A summer resort by the mid-1800s, the village had an electric railway to Waterbury from 1897 to 1932, and by the 1930s the CCC was cutting ski trails on Mount Mansfield.

moments.title: Mount Mansfield
moments.text: Vermont's highest mountain, at 4,393 feet, looks from the east like a long human profile with forehead, nose and chin, and the chin is the summit.
